sources.title: Which AI agents work with Enjoy? — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Supported agent list: Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity and Muse Code; OpenCode supports local models. Agent processes keep their own accounts.

sources.title: What agents can do inside Enjoy — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Agents have product tools for conversations, docs, instructions, workflows, processes and previews. Cross-project requests return results and require approval if the recipient has broader permission; fan-out is bounded at 15 conversations per request.

sources.title: Run one of your agents' skills — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Native agent skills and supported plugin skills are listed with origin; other agents can receive eligible skill instructions. Files are re-read at send time; errors block the send.

sources.title: Choose what your agent can do without asking — Operating Manual
sources.finding: The selected coding harness enforces its permission mode; rejected modes stop instead of being broadened. Modes and changing them vary by harness.

sources.title: Choose where a project's conversations are stored — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Project records are stored separately from project files in app data; relocation copies and checks them. Removing a project or resetting the app does not delete those records.

sources.title: Keep a project synced across your computers — Operating Manual
sources.finding: History, docs, workflows and instructions synchronize between online computers using the same Git identity; active runtime, worktrees, drafts, schedules and permission settings do not migrate.

sources.title: Limit how many agents work at once — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Per-project concurrent-agent limit defaults unlimited and may be set up to 30; FIFO waiting with manual Start now override; waiting approval frees a slot.

sources.title: Send a message when another conversation finishes — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Queued messages can wait on another conversation finishing its turn or being marked completed. Failure/approval pauses keep them waiting; cycles are rejected. Agents can queue these messages visibly.

sources.title: What conversation statuses mean — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Conversation status includes working, watching, queued, needs input, out of usage, stopped, failed, completed, snoozed and could not load. Inbox aggregates project attention.

sources.title: How Enjoy keeps your unsent messages — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Unsent desktop drafts persist with their projects; browser drafts last only while page open; iPhone drafts persist locally with duplicate-send uncertainty notice.

sources.title: See and restore a doc's versions — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Agent edits preserve prior human text and changed text; versions show attribution, time, conversation and diff. Restore keeps previous state; newest 40 versions retained, fewer for long docs and none above about 200000 characters.

sources.title: Schedule a workflow — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Recurring or one-time schedules run on the awake signed-in computer, with timezones and cron. Overlapping or human-blocked runs are skipped; missed time does not accumulate a backlog.

sources.title: Link workflows so one runs after another — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Workflow references follow latest linked instructions in the same conversation and agent. Cyclic or deleted references require review and stop execution.

sources.title: Try ideas side by side in worktrees — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Agents create Git worktrees on separate branches under .worktrees, retaining the same conversation; ignored files and uncommitted changes do not follow. Worktrees are not runtime sandboxes.

sources.title: Merge a worktree into your project — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Merge sends a normal agent message immediately, without a separate confirmation. Agent handles conflicts or asks; the worktree remains afterward.

sources.title: Review the changes an agent made — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Committed reply changes have a parent-relative diff and commit selector; narrow browser and iPhone views differ. Large diffs have limits and binary files show a notice.

sources.title: What to do when an agent runs out of usage — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Default usage-limit response switches to another available agent account, then waits and retries after reset. Other settings wait or stop; unknown reset times retry after about 15 minutes up to hourly. Provider request rate errors need manual retry.

sources.title: See what a conversation used — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Desktop Claude Code turns expose conversation and last-message tokens, API-price comparison, model requests and working time. API price is not subscription billing; other agents and phone/web do not supply these turn metrics.

sources.title: Working on someone else's computer — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Shared project access supports live conversations, sender attribution and presence. Can work members can prompt, but only owner or full personal devices approve tools; host must be online.

sources.title: Change what a teammate can access — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Per-project No access, Can view and Can work permissions apply across devices; changes/revocation stop active work. This does not establish organization SSO or provisioning.

sources.title: Store your Enjoy sign-in in the system keychain — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Enjoy credentials are stored in an unencrypted local file by default; OS keychain is opt-in per computer. Coding-agent account stores remain separate.

sources.title: Delete all application data — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Reset stops active work and removes app preferences, pairing, signin and logs, but retains project records and independently installed coding-agent accounts.

sources.title: Turn usage statistics on or off — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Desktop usage reports count named actions with random installation ID, version, OS and plan. In-app Share usage statistics disables reports and clears queued events; re-enabling generates a new ID. Unsent events older than 30 days are dropped. Phone/web do not send their own reports.

sources.title: Enjoy's plan and price — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Current subscription includes one computer with extra-computer monthly charges and separate agent billing. Seven-day card-required trial; grandfathered free installations and pre-November-8 subscriptions retain different terms.

sources.title: Give agents a token or key without showing it to them — Operating Manual
sources.finding: Named project environment secrets are injected into tools and redacted in output; agents may use them without a separate approval in any permission mode.
